text:
morgan: Heads up — I have a repro for a KV cache paging issue that causes long-context memory growth + eviction thrash. Seen on H100 and MI250x.

morgan: Repro steps: run longctx workload (seq_len ~32k tokens) with paged-kv enabled, low cache size (config: cache_pages=1024, page_size=64KB), and heavy prefix reuse. After ~20-30 minutes GPU resident memory climbs steadily.

morgan: Quick traces attached below (snips). Notable pattern: pages repeatedly flip between "GPU resident" and "host resident" without steady reuse, evict_count ~ remap_count (~1:1).

morgan: ```
TRACE kvcache: evict 1372 remap 1370 reuse_hit 5 spill_ms 12
PT: fold_ops=1401 unmap_ops=1399 remap_ops=1400
GPU 0 resident_mb=24500 -> 25200 -> 24600 -> 25300
```

sree: Which kernel path are you hitting for paged-attn? Is this the tiled-gemm fallback or the vectorized GEMM?

morgan: On H100 we get tiled-gemm optimized path most of the time. On MI250x it falls back to the generic attention kernel ~20% of the time because of alignment rounding; that coincides with higher remap churn.

eva: Any evidence of double-free / stale PT entries or just high churn? Could be allocator fragmentation + LRU misordering.

morgan: I instrumented the PT owner/epoch and saw a sequence where a page gets evicted, remapped shortly after by a different stream, then evicted again by the background reclaimer. Owner pointer toggles between gpuA/gpuB rapidly. Not a double-free but a reuse oscillation.

morgan: Snip from the debug log: ```
[15823.12] page 0x7f9c... owner=gpu0 epoch=102 evict->host
[15823.13] page 0x7f9c... remap<-gpu1 epoch=103
[15823.14] page 0x7f9c... evict->host epoch=104
```

dave: That looks like a race in the eviction heuristic + the streaming kernel's prefetch window. If a stream prefetches pages that are still being reclaimed, you get immediate remaps. Could be our prefetch ahead window is too aggressive for longctx.

sree: What does telemetry for reuse_window show? Any long tails?

morgan: reuse_window distribution (minutes): median 0.2, 90p 0.9, 99p 12. But the pages that thrash show reuse_window ~0.02 then 0.03 then 0.01 — basically bouncing.

eva: Interesting. Could it be the free-list LIFO -> causes locality but unlucky placement means sibling pages are far and cause fragmentation?

morgan: I also saw free-list fragmentation growth: free_chunks count grows while total free bytes remain similar, suggesting lots of small holes. On MI250x allocator uses 128KB slab buckets by default; our page folding creates many partial-slab survivors.

morgan: Perf counters from the host-side pager: page_faults/sec spikes correlated with increase in GPU memcpy bandwidth: 2.2GB/s -> 7.8GB/s during thrash periods.

ops-bot: deploybot: Added kvcache/evict-guard experimental flag to the smoke cluster (off by default).

dave: Proposed quick mitigations: reduce prefetch_ahead from 16 -> 6 for longctx profiles; add a short backoff when a page gets remapped within X ms of eviction (coalesce flips); and change free-list allocation to prefer reusing contiguous slabs.

sree: Backoff idea makes sense. We should be careful with latency SLO impact — coalescing can increase first-token latency if we over-hold pages. Maybe only trigger backoff when we detect flip pattern > N times in T window.

morgan: I pushed a prototype that: 1) tracks recent evict/remap pairs per-page (tiny ring buffer), 2) if flips > 3 in 5s mark page "hot-oscillating" and treat as temporarily pinned for 50ms.

morgan: Quick benchmark on H100 (longctx synthetic): before: steady mem +23% over 30m, avg eviction rate 120/s. After prototype: mem delta reduced to +3%, eviction rate 18/s, 95p latency +1.8% (small).

eva: Promising. Did you test with quantized kernels that change memory access patterns? MI250x may need a different threshold.

morgan: Yes, MI250x required threshold 2 flips -> 30ms pin to get similar improvement. Probably due to PCIe/InfinityFabric remap latency differences.

dave: Next steps: 1) land metric to detect page-folding pattern in prod telemetry, 2) run controlled A/B on staging with prefetch reduction + flip-backoff, 3) follow-up to change allocator to reduce partial-slab fragmentation.

sree: Also add a per-arch knob: prefetch_window & flip_backoff_ms profiles for H100, A100, MI250x.

morgan: I will open a PR with the prototype and a perf run summary. Attaching perf dump + small repro script in the PR.

dave: Thanks. If anyone wants to triage quicker, run `./tools/kv-repro --longctx --pages=1024 --arch=mi250x` and look for remap_rate > 10/s.

morgan: thanks all :thumbsup:

ops-bot: incidentbot: Created incident-4898765432 for KV cache thrash investigation.
